answer: An AI marketplace selling garden plans, from cedar planting to irrigation, can require each seller to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before receiving one unit of bidding capacity. Creating extra identities grants no free capacity: every account needs its own bond. An attacker running 10,000 accounts must immobilize $1 million for a month, sacrificing liquidity and interest. This prevents a cheap spiral of fake accounts from multiplying market access.
